## Summative Inquiry Prompt 核心探究问题

::: {.callout-note title="Central Inquiry Prompt 总结性评估核心问题" icon=false}
**"To what extent did Classical Mediterranean systems of governance represent progress given their continuous dependence on slavery?"**

“鉴于古典地中海文明对奴隶制度的持续依赖，其治理体系在多大程度上代表了人类社会的进步？”
:::

- **Primary Focus 重点范围:** Classical Greece (Athenian {{< vocab "democracy" >}} / Spartan oligarchy) and Ancient Rome ({{< vocab "republic" >}} / Twelve Tables).
- **Optional Baseline 可选对比基准:** Unit 1 River Valley Civilizations (Mesopotamia / Egypt).

::: notes
Read the prompt aloud together. Emphasize that "To what extent" requires weighing two sides: real political/legal breakthroughs for citizens vs. systemic dependence on forced labor and exclusion.
:::

## Mingwan 4-Band Rubric Overview 评定量规概览 {.subslide}

| Band 等级 | Crit B: Investigating 探究 (Booklet) | Crit D: Thinking Critically 批判性思维 | Crit C: Communicating 沟通表达 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **EX (90–100%)** | {{< vocab "formulate" text="Formulates" >}} nuanced RQ & thesis; rich balanced book + text evidence; deep source {{< vocab "evaluate" text="evaluation" >}} | {{< vocab "analyse" text="Analyzes" >}} governance vs. slavery contradiction, perspectives & counter-claim | Persuasive academic English; sophisticated transitions; full {{< vocab "document" text="citations" >}} |
| **PR (75–89%)** | Clear RQ & arguable thesis; accurate evidence from books & texts; checklist complete | Clearly {{< vocab "explain" text="explains" >}} governance progress & slavery limits using specific evidence | Clear formal English; follows essay blueprint; accurate source list |
| **DE (60–74%)** | Basic claim; partial checklist; relies mostly on one source or descriptive facts | {{< vocab "describe" text="Describes" >}} facts separately without {{< vocab "analyse" text="analyzing" >}} the contradiction | Uneven paragraph structure; limited transitions; incomplete citations |
| **EM (1–59%)** | Unclear or missing RQ/thesis; minimal source evidence recorded | Unsupported personal opinions without historical evidence | Fragmented writing; minimal academic vocabulary; no citations |

## Week 1 · Lesson 1: Prompt, Thesis & Research {background-color="#003477"}

**第1周 · 第1课：审题拆解、中心论点与史料收集**

- Booklet Section 1 (Steps 1.1 – 1.4)
- Criterion B: Investigating (Strands i–iii)

::: notes
Lesson 1 (50 min):
- 10 min: Deconstruct prompt & model Research Question + Thesis frame.
- 30 min: Library books & class texts research log (Sources 1–4).
- 10 min: Check claim-evidence alignment & log Lesson 1 tracker.
:::

## Lesson 1 · Step 1.1: Deconstruct the Prompt 拆解题目

In **Booklet Step 1.1**, we {{< vocab "analyse" text="analyze" >}} and break the prompt into **three key parts**:

1. **"To what extent…"** 在多大程度上…… *(Measuring how much real progress was achieved)*
2. **"…systems of governance represent progress…"** 治理体系代表进步…… *(Breakthroughs in citizen rights, voting & written law)*
3. **"…given their continuous dependence on slavery?"** 鉴于对奴隶制的持续依赖？ *(How forced labor & exclusion limited that progress)*

::: notes
This overview slide introduces the three parts of Step 1.1. Press Down (↓) to walk students through each of the three rows in their Step 1.1 table one by one, or press Right (→) to move straight to Step 1.2.
:::

## Step 1.1 (Part 1): "To what extent…" 在多大程度上 {.subslide}

::: {.callout-note title="Row 1 Guiding Question 第一行思考引导" icon=false}
**How much real progress was achieved? Was it major progress, partial/limited progress, or progress only for a privileged minority?**

究竟实现了多少真正的进步？是巨大的进步、部分的/有限的进步，还是仅仅属于少数特权公民的进步？
:::

- **"To what extent"** means your answer cannot just be *"Yes"* or *"No."*
- You must {{< vocab "evaluate" >}} and weigh **both sides** on a scale:
  - **Side A:** Political & legal breakthroughs for free male {{< vocab "citizen" text="citizens" >}}
  - **Side B:** Systemic dependence on slavery and exclusion of the majority

## Step 1.1 (Part 2): "…governance represent progress…" 治理进步 {.subslide}

::: {.callout-tip title="Row 2 Guiding Question 第二行思考引导" icon=false}
**Which system(s) will you {{< vocab "analyse" text="analyze" >}}? How did voting, checks & balances, or written law protect citizens?**

你将分析哪些制度？公民投票、权力制衡或成文法如何保障公民权利？
:::

- **Athenian {{< vocab "democracy" >}} 雅典民主制:** Direct {{< vocab "vote" text="voting" >}} in the {{< vocab "assembly" >}} (*Ecclesia*), civic participation.
- **Roman {{< vocab "republic" >}} 罗马共和制:** Elected {{< vocab "consul" text="consuls" >}}, the {{< vocab "senate" >}}, tribunes, and **checks and balances 权力制衡**.
- **Rule of Law 法治进步:** The **Twelve Tables 《十二铜表法》** — publicly written laws and due process.
- *(Optional Baseline 可选对比)* Compare to Unit 1 River Valley kings (Hammurabi / Pharaohs).

## Step 1.1 (Part 3): "…dependence on slavery?" 奴隶制依赖 {.subslide}

::: {.callout-warning title="Row 3 Guiding Question 第三行思考引导" icon=false}
**How did Athens, Sparta, and/or Rome depend on forced labor? Who else was excluded?**

雅典、斯巴达和/或罗马如何依赖强制劳动？还有谁被排斥在外（女性、外邦人）？
:::

- **Athens 雅典:** Enslaved workers in the **Laurium silver mines 银矿** and domestic households gave citizens free time to participate in politics.
- **Sparta 斯巴达:** State-owned **helots 希洛人** outnumbered Spartan citizens roughly **8 to 1**, farming all the food so Spartans could train for war.
- **Rome 古罗马:** Up to **33% enslaved population** working on huge estates (**latifundia 大庄园**), mines, and as {{< vocab "gladiator" text="gladiators" >}}.
- **Civic Exclusion 公民权排斥:** Women, foreigners (*metics*), and enslaved people could not vote.

## Lesson 1 · Step 1.2: Thesis Statement Frame 中心论点模板

{{< vocab "use" text="Use" >}} this frame to {{< vocab "formulate" >}} an arguable **"To what extent"** claim in English:

::: {.callout-tip title="Model Thesis Frame 中心论点句型模板" icon=false}
*"Although Classical Mediterranean governance in **[Athens / the Roman Republic / Greece and Rome]** represented significant political and legal progress through **[citizen voting / checks and balances / the Twelve Tables]**, this progress was fundamentally limited because **[these societies continuously depended on institutional slavery and excluded the majority of the population from civic rights]**."*
:::

::: {.small-note}
中文逻辑：尽管古典地中海文明通过……取得了显著政治与法律进步，但这种进步在根本上是有限的，因为这些社会持续依赖制度化的奴隶制，并将大多数人口排斥在公民权利之外。
:::

## Lesson 2 · Source Value & Limitation 史料价值与局限

In **Step 1.4**, {{< vocab "evaluate" >}} **one** library book or primary source you used:

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-note title="1. Source Value 史料价值" icon=false}
Why is this source helpful for your essay?

- Provides specific laws, statistics, or historian {{< vocab "analyse" text="analysis" >}} of {{< vocab "democracy" >}}, the {{< vocab "republic" >}}, or slavery.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-warning title="2. Source Limitation 史料局限性" icon=false}
What is one limitation of this source?

- Primary sources were often written by elite male {{< vocab "citizen" text="citizens" >}}, leaving out the voices of enslaved people and women.
:::
:::
::::

## Lesson 2 · TEEL Paragraph Blueprint 主体段结构蓝图

| Part | Role in Paragraph 段落作用 | Sentence Starter 英文句型支架 |
|---|---|---|
| **T** · Topic Sentence | State the main point of the paragraph | *"A major political breakthrough in [Athens/Rome] was…"* |
| **E** · Evidence | {{< vocab "document" text="Cite" >}} specific laws, numbers, or facts + source | *"According to [Author, p. xx], the Twelve Tables…"* |
| **E** · {{< vocab "explain" text="Explanation" >}} | {{< vocab "analyse" text="Analyze" >}} **how/why** this shows progress or limits | *"This empowered citizens by… / From an enslaved worker's view…"* |
| **L** · Link | Connect back to your "to what extent" thesis | *"Therefore, civic progress remained restricted to a minority."* |

## Sentence Starters: Body 1 & Body 2 英文学术句型库 {.subslide}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-note title="Body 1: Governance Progress 治理进步" icon=false}
- *"A major political breakthrough in [Athens/Rome] was…"*
- *"According to [Source/Author, p. xx], the Twelve Tables established…"*
- *"Compared to earlier monarchies, this system empowered {{< vocab "citizen" text="citizens" >}} by…"*
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-warning title="Body 2: Contradiction of Slavery 奴隶制局限" icon=false}
- *"However, this civic progress was severely undermined by…"*
- *"Despite these legal protections for citizens, [Athens/Rome] remained dependent on…"*
- *"From the perspective of an enslaved laborer / Spartan helot…"*
:::
:::
::::

## Week 1 · Lesson 3: Counter-Claim & Conclusion {background-color="#003477"}

**第1周 · 第3课：标准B最终确认、反方观点段与结论段**

Lesson 3 (50 min):

- Differentiated instruction: Advanced Path writes Counter-Claim & Rebuttal; Standard Path deepens perspective analysis in Body 1 & 2, then all students write Conclusion.

## Lesson 3 · Two Pathways 进阶反方段与标准深化

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-tip title="Advanced Path 进阶路径 (Body 3)" icon=false}
**Counter-Claim & Rebuttal 反方观点与批驳**

1. **{{< vocab "formulate" text="Formulate" >}} Counter-Claim:** *"Some historians argue that judged by ancient standards, [democracy / law] was still revolutionary because…"*
2. **{{< vocab "justify" text="Justify" >}} Rebuttal:** *"Nevertheless, this overlooks the reality that citizen freedom was directly financed by enslaved labor…"*
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-note title="Standard Path 标准路径 (Deepen Body 1 & 2)" icon=false}
**Deepen Perspective & Citations 深化分析**

1. Check that Body 1 and Body 2 both {{< vocab "document" text="cite" >}} **specific page numbers** from library books and class texts.
2. Explicitly {{< vocab "analyse" text="analyze" >}} and compare the lived experience of a free male {{< vocab "citizen" >}} vs. an enslaved laborer or helot.
:::
:::
::::

## Lesson 3 · Final Paragraph: The Conclusion 结论段

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="62%"}
Your conclusion must {{< vocab "synthesize" >}} your essay in **three steps**:

1. **Restate your thesis** in fresh words (do not copy-paste).
2. **{{< vocab "evaluate" text="Evaluate" >}} & weigh both sides:** Balance civic/legal achievements against the human cost of chattel slavery and helotry.
3. **Final "To What Extent" Judgment:** Give a clear, reasoned historical verdict.
:::
::: {.column width="38%"}
{{< timer 30 >}}
:::
::::

## Lesson 4 · The 6 Peer Audit Checkpoints 互评六大核查点 {.subslide}

| Checkpoint 核查点 | What to Look For 互评检查重点 |
|---|---|
| **1. Thesis Clarity (Crit D)** | Does the Intro end with a clear *"to what extent"* claim linking governance and slavery? |
| **2. Governance Evidence (Crit B/D)** | Does Body 1 {{< vocab "document" text="cite" >}} specific laws/facts from library books or class texts? |
| **3. Slavery & Perspectives (Crit D)** | Does Body 2 {{< vocab "analyse" text="analyze" >}} and contrast the perspective of a free citizen vs. an enslaved worker/helot? |
| **4. Counter-Claim (Adv · Crit D)** | *(If Advanced Path)* Does Body 3 state a fair counter-argument and {{< vocab "justify" >}} its rebuttal with evidence? |
| **5. Structure & Transitions (Crit C)** | Are paragraphs organized with analytical transitions (*however, whereas, despite*)? |
| **6. Source Citations (Crit C)** | Are book titles/authors and page numbers explicitly {{< vocab "document" text="documented" >}} inside the paragraphs? |

## Lesson 5 · Upgrading DE → PR / EX 提分关键策略

| Area 维度 | Developing (DE · 60–74%) | Proficient / Exceeding (PR/EX · 75–100%) |
|---|---|---|
| **Analysis (Crit D)** | {{< vocab "list" text="Lists" >}} facts about government and slavery separately | {{< vocab "analyse" text="Analyzes" >}} the **contradiction**: how citizen freedom depended on enslaved labor |
| **Perspectives (Crit D)** | Mentions only one viewpoint | Contrasts **free citizen** vs. **enslaved person / helot / woman** |
| **Transitions (Crit C)** | Basic connectors (*First, Second, Also*) | Analytical transitions (*However, Whereas, Despite these legal protections*) |
| **Citations (Crit C)** | No page numbers or source names | In-text citations `(Author, p. xx)` + {{< vocab "document" text="documented" >}} **Works Cited** list |
